bricks.name: WriteBackExtreme Write-back Extension
bricks.description: The flagship Enterprise-only write-back product: a Tableau dashboard extension (also shipped as a Power BI visual) that lets planners, controllers and operations staff enter forecasts, budgets, targets, comments, corrections, survey answers, task lists and approvals directly in the dashboard and store them in the customer's own governed database, without Excel round-trips. Data never leaves the customer's environment: WriteBackExtreme runs on the customer's Windows or Linux server (one-click installer, no internet required) or in a personal cloud environment for the 30-day trial. Every change carries who, what and when, can be rolled back, and is governed by SSO and role management so that only the right people write to the right columns. Common use cases are planning and forecasting, what-if scenarios, data correction, annotations and approvals; Pfizer reports that everybody uses the dashboard made with WriteBackExtreme because it is straightforward and intuitive.

bricks.name: InputTables Data Entry Grid
bricks.description: Excel-like data entry inside a SuperTable: users type in cells, add comments per cell, and extend the table with dynamic columns (for example a new scenario or month) without a developer touching the dashboard. InputTables is the light-weight companion of WriteBackExtreme for planners and analysts who want spreadsheet ergonomics with governed storage: every cell edit is written through the write-back backend into the customer's database with the same audit trail, rollback and role model. Available for Tableau and, since 2022, for Power BI through Microsoft AppSource. Typical use: budget and forecast entry, target setting, data quality corrections and survey-style collection inside an existing dashboard.

bricks.name: FinanceTables Financial Statements
bricks.description: Finance-grade statements inside the dashboard: profit and loss, balance sheet, budget-versus-actual and management statements built from an account hierarchy with sign rules, subtotals, variance columns and drill-through to the underlying rows. FinanceTables gives FP&A analysts and controllers the layout they expect from a finance system (indented account trees, bold subtotals, percentage-of-revenue columns, period comparisons) on top of Tableau data, and exports the statement to Excel or a scheduled PDF. It reuses the SuperTables grid for rendering and, when combined with InputTables and WriteBackExtreme, turns the statement into a budget entry surface.

bricks.name: SuperTables Interactive Grid
bricks.description: The most widely deployed extension: an Excel-like grid inside Tableau, Power BI and Looker Studio that lets viewers pivot, group, sort, filter, resize and reorder columns, apply conditional formatting, add formulas and totals, export to Excel and save personalised views, all without asking for a new dashboard. A server-side row model streams millions of rows on demand so the grid stays responsive where a native table would not, and generative fill lets users describe a new column in plain language. A Post Holdings senior director with 1,000+ Tableau users says SuperTables made Tableau much more accessible to people used to Excel. SuperTables is also the host for InputTables and FinanceTables.
